data.body:
Epic plan-review (job 1788385138...731a5ae3) completed with verdict BLOCK (1 blocking, 7 advisory) against sha 8a38aa76. 

Blocking finding (criterion T8, decomposition/no-fire predicate): the epic claimed the sidecar corpus lets you state "which criteria fired and which stayed silent," but the sidecar persists only findings that FIRED — so a no-fire (expect: pass) case cannot distinguish "criterion silent" from "criterion never routed" without an explicit cohort-membership predicate. Grounded: verified sidecar.py:649-717 `_slim` writes a per-FINDING record with a per-finding `cohort` set (the criterion-id set co-resident in the finder call); missing cohort must be treated as unknown, never empty.

Remediation applied to epic description (edit_ticket): (1) Context now states silence is evidence only via the per-finding cohort set; (2) new "No-fire evidence predicate" paragraph in Approach — admit a plan as no-fire evidence for C only when C is in the cohort set of some finding on that plan AND no finding cites C, skip missing-cohort rows; (3) new acceptance criterion for the predicate with a 3-case synthetic-corpus pytest; (4) child-decomposition attribution (selector owns predicate, emitter transcribes). Trimmed prose to stay under the 8,000-char plan-review admission cap (final 7,933). This predicate will need to be reflected in the 549b selector and 092c emitter child plans too.

Re-running the epic plan-review gate now.
